A repeated Fling stack id was accepted again inside ten minutes.
A Fling offer that broke a rule reached a prompt instead of being declined first.
Fling arrivals landed outside Downloads/Fling, or in Downloads without access.
A Fling peer stayed listed after ten seconds, or was shown under its advertised name once paired.
A Fling flick fired below its sensitivity threshold or picked the wrong target.
The persisted Fling Shelf record grew past 500, was world-readable, or overwrote a file it could not read.
A Fling offer was sent before every hash was ready.
Fling accepted more than eight connections or two transfers from one peer.
Fling advertised or listened beyond what the visibility setting allows.
A Mac that was never paired got past the Fling TLS handshake.
Pairing two Macs did not give the same code, or a stack of four items including 50 MB did not arrive with matching hashes and a Shelf record.
The open Fling pairing port accepted an offer from a stranger.
A Fling name with a path climb was accepted or wrote a file outside the stack folder.
A cancelled or corrupted Fling transfer left a partial or final file, or blocked the next send.
The Fling key was stored outside the Keychain, or Remove left a key behind.
Fling Shelf items lost their origin, stack or verified mark, or did not survive a relaunch.
The Fling glow showed with its Settings switch off, or reused the AirDrop colours.
The AirDrop and screenshot watcher picked up files Fling wrote into its own folder.
The Info.plist lacked the Local Network reason or the declared Bonjour type.
Fling sent without a gesture: on a failure, an arrival, an offer or a change of peers.
Fling could be turned on by a settings import or by default, or its Settings section was missing from the live window.
The Shelf did not offer Turn on while Fling was off, or a drop onto an avatar did not send that item to that Mac with the drop gesture.
The accept card did not answer the receive machine, or sixty seconds without an answer did not decline.
Files that arrived together did not collapse into one stack cell, a saved stack lost files, or a drag out moved them instead of copying.
Ask each time did not prompt a paired Mac, Clipboard or a missing Downloads grant wrote into Downloads/Fling, or a link opened without the switch.
A floating paper took focus, left the screen, or closing it removed the file from the Shelf.
A send over 2 GB went out without saying so.
A pairing was stored on the starting Mac as soon as the peer confirmed, with no confirmation from its own person.
Expired or dropped pairing attempts, and ids rotated from one address, were never counted toward the mute.
A paired Mac could claim another paired Mac's id in its hello.
Huge declared sizes overflowed a sum and trapped the receiver.
A bidi or format character in a received name passed validation.
A numbered or folder name could pass 255 bytes, or a case-only clash overwrote a file.
The intake watcher skipped any folder named Fling, not only Zeus's own receiving folders.
A received link to a loopback, private or local address opened by itself.
The frame decoder copied the rest of its buffer per frame, and accepted a chunk with no data.
Silent pairing connections could lock out transfers or later pairing.
Bytes promised to a running stack were not counted against the next offer.
Stopping an endpoint left transfers without an end event.
Every keystroke in the device name rebuilt both listeners.
Pairing an already paired id silently replaced its key.
An answer to a pairing prompt went to every pairing session.
A new card could be answered by a click in its first second.
A Mac that refused a stored key was not told to pair again.
The pairing answer did not name the Mac it was for.
Received files carried no quarantine mark.
A link host written with leading zeros, octal, hex, decimal or full width digits was judged public.
A wildcard-IP DNS name, or a name spelling a private address, was judged public.
The address that was checked was not the address handed to the browser.
A failed attempt that never showed a code could mute the id it claimed.
An inbound pairing attempt from a paired Mac showed a banner or revealed which ids are paired.
A dropped pairing was counted twice toward the mute.
A file whose quarantine mark could not be set still came into view.
A start from the other talk key reached the owner while a turn was open, so one hold or one hands-free turn could open the microphone twice.
Right Option pressed with a letter at typing speed (an accent) started a talk turn: the listen sound, speech stopped and the microphone on.
Left Option started the second talk key, which belongs to Right Option only.
Control joining a held Right Option turn let the Control-Option start fire after the cancel, so one hold opened two turns.
Right Option ended a Control-Option hands-free turn, though only the key that opened a hands-free turn may end it.
The second talk key default was written to the settings or read as the owner's choice, so it could not yield to another key or be reset.
The second talk key kept Right Option when the talk, dictation, Polyglot or pointing key, Chat on Option-Space or VoiceOver already used it, so one hold opened the microphone twice or typed.
The second talk key was not compared with the tiling chords, so a keymap that binds Option alone and the voice key both acted on one hold.
Test runs left more than 10,000 empty settings files in the owner's ~/Library/Preferences: throwaway suites named zeus.x.<UUID> outlive removePersistentDomain.
An async onboarding test left the process-wide snapshot flag on while it slept, so settings tests that ran meanwhile skipped their writes and failed at random.
The Record page showed a Mic level row while recording although microphone capture is greyed out as Soon.
The notch permission hint was cut off mid-word (Turn it on to use fa...) because it was a single fixed-width line.
Settings pop-ups were a fixed 153 points wide, so Control-Option and Automatic (best working voice) showed with an ellipsis.
The Languages onboarding step has no visual, so its column was centred in the window and its note ran into the Set up later button.
The Face presence hint sat left of the row titles and said Privacy and Security where macOS says Privacy & Security.
With VoiceOver on, the open notch panel closed 0.2 s after the pointer left it, so a VoiceOver user could not switch tabs: VoiceOver's cursor is not the pointer.
With AirPods as the microphone, the headset switched profile when the talk key went down, the audio engine stopped and was never restarted, so every talk turn heard nothing.
Every talk-key press started the Ultron output engine, which pulled AirPods back to the playback profile while the microphone was opening, so the two engines fought over the Bluetooth link.
Talk turns ignored the microphone chosen in Dictation settings and always used the system input, so an AirPods default was used even when another microphone was picked.
Test runs wrote lines into the owner's real ~/Library/Logs/Zeus/voice.log, mixing test output into the evidence used to debug live voice turns.
Every ElevenLabs 401 said quota exceeded, so a bad key and used-up credits gave the same notice and the owner could not tell whether to paste a new key or wait.
Used-up ElevenLabs credits were reported as a rejected key, so the notice told the owner to check a key that was fine.
Talk turns could not be told to use the Mac's own microphone, so a connected Bluetooth headset always switched profile for every talk turn, and a chosen input that was unplugged was not handled.
Talk turns reused the Dictation microphone, so choosing a microphone for dictation silently moved talk turns, and talk had no choice of its own.
With Right Option as the talk key, Settings warned that the second talk key was off and told the owner to record another key, although the owner never set a second key and wants Right Option only.
The quiet Off for a default second key must not hide the warning when the owner recorded a clashing key, or the key would be off with no explanation.
